stem: A liver recipient calls reporting bright red blood on the toilet paper after a bowel movement. According to urgent-contact education, how should the coordinator classify this symptom?

options.text: An urgent matter because rectal bleeding is a potential source requiring prompt team contact
A non-urgent matter to address at the next routine refill call
An expected finding that never requires transplant team notification
A reason to permanently stop all immunosuppression without team guidance

explanation.rationale_correct: Bleeding from potential sources including rectal, oral, wound, or ostomy sites is listed as an urgent reason to contact the transplant team.

rationale_incorrect.B: Rectal bleeding is categorized among urgent matters, not routine non-urgent contacts.
rationale_incorrect.C: Bleeding after transplant requires prompt evaluation rather than assumed normalcy.
rationale_incorrect.D: Bleeding prompts team contact and coordinated evaluation, not independent immunosuppression cessation.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → §h. Communication → iii. Urgent matters → Bleeding

stem: When planning discharge antimicrobial teaching for a kidney recipient, what determines the need for cytomegalovirus (CMV) prophylaxis?

options.text: Recipient and donor CMV IgG status at the time of transplantation
Whether the recipient prefers brand-name versus generic immunosuppressants
CMV prophylaxis is never used after kidney transplantation

explanation.rationale_correct: Discharge medication education includes that CMV prophylaxis is determined by recipient and donor CMV IgG status at transplantation, which guides need and duration.

rationale_incorrect.B: CMV prophylaxis decisions are based on serologic risk, not dietary preferences.
rationale_incorrect.C: Brand versus generic preference does not determine CMV prophylaxis protocols.
rationale_incorrect.D: CMV prophylaxis is commonly individualized based on donor/recipient CMV status.

stem: A kidney recipient on cyclosporine reports gum overgrowth and requests a switch to tacrolimus. Which adverse effect pairing is consistent with standard CNI references?

options.text: Cyclosporine is associated with gingival hypertrophy; switching to tacrolimus may be considered for this cosmetic side effect
Cyclosporine never causes gingival changes; only tacrolimus does
Gingival hypertrophy requires immediate graft nephrectomy
CNIs have no cosmetic or mucosal side effects

explanation.rationale_correct: References note cyclosporine-associated gingival hypertrophy as a common reason to switch to tacrolimus, alongside other CNI cosmetic effects such as hirsutism.

rationale_incorrect.B: Gingival hypertrophy is described with cyclosporine, not exclusively with tacrolimus.
rationale_incorrect.C: Gingival overgrowth is managed medically and may prompt CNI switching, not nephrectomy.
rationale_incorrect.D: CNIs have recognized cosmetic and mucosal adverse effects.

stem: A kidney recipient with stable graft function is 14 months post-transplant. According to long-term follow-up references, what clinic visit interval is generally recommended during the second post-transplant year?

options.text: No follow-up after the first anniversary
Daily in-person visits at the transplant center

explanation.rationale_correct: After monthly visits through the first year, follow-up references recommend every 1 to 2 months during the second year for functioning grafts, then every 3 to 4 months thereafter.

rationale_incorrect.B: Biennial or less frequent visits do not match the recommended second-year schedule.
rationale_incorrect.C: Transplant follow-up continues throughout the second year and beyond.
rationale_incorrect.D: Daily center visits are not the described long-term surveillance interval.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 11, Post-transplant Long-term Management → follow-up visit frequency paragraph
primary_anchor.quote_hint: For the next year, the visits should be every 1 to 2 months

references.locator: Ch. 11 → follow-up visit frequency (second year: every 1–2 months); PDF p. 302 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).
